Subject: MAP & close sequencing: MSA/DPA/order form dependencies for Novus pilot

Hi Sophie / Novus procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the pilot looked like a great fit. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (novus_map_v1.xlsx) that maps evaluation milestones to legal/procurement gates. Key asks here:

- Can you confirm preferred DPA turnaround (we penciled 5 business days for your legal team)?
- Does procurement need an executed DPA before PO/order form is issued, or is a redlined DPA + PO acceptable to start provisioning?
- Any blackout dates for signature (internal review weeks, exec vacations) between 11/20 and 12/10?

We tried to sequence items to reduce blockers: initial evaluation sign-off -> DPA review -> final MSA redline-window (parallel) -> order form & PO issuance -> signature. Attachment also includes a short "MSA summary" (redwood_msa_summary_v1.pdf) that highlights clauses we expect will commonly be redlined.

If this sequencing works for Novus, we propose the following milestone dates (draft):
- Evaluation acceptance: 11/30
- DPA initial comments due: 12/07
- MSA redline window (parallel): 12/07–12/14
- Final sign & PO: target 12/17

Please let us know which items you need reordered/merged. Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow to align owners.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0143

Tessa — thanks, the MAP is helpful. A few quick notes from procurement/legal side:

- Procurement prefers an executed DPA before we issue a PO for pilot data access. We can accept a redlined MSA in parallel but need DPA signed first.
- Our legal lead Amit will own DPA review; typical turnaround is 7 business days, but we can try to hit 5 if the clause table is tight.
- We have an internal security review scheduled 11/22–11/24 (team offsite) so anything routed during that window may be delayed.

Two asks: can you provide a one-page clause map (DPA vs MSA items) called "dpa_clause_table_v2.docx" that summarizes the must-have DPA obligations vs negotiable MSA terms? That will help speed Amit's review.

If Novus agrees to DPA-first sequencing, the timeline in your draft looks achievable with the following tweak: DPA comments due 12/09 (give Amit the full week after their offsite).

Sophie Tan
Head of Strategic Procurement, Novus Health

Hi Sophie / team — looping in high-level legal sequencing so everyone has clarity on gating and owners. This is from legal's POV and intended to be prescriptive to avoid rework: 

Proposed sequencing (legal -> procurement):
1) DPA first: Novus signs DPA (data handling + SID/incident SLAs) — owner: Amit Rao (Novus).
2) Security questionnaire/evidence collection (concurrent with DPA comments) — owner: Procurement and Security; target evidence list in the MAP.
3) MSA redlines: Redwood legal will accept redlines; we can prioritize key commercial terms (term, termination, indemnity cap) to keep negotiation narrow — owner: Laura Bennett (Redwood).
4) Order form / PO issuance: Procurement releases PO once DPA is executed and commercial terms are agreed in order form — owner: Sophie / Procurement.
5) Signature: final handoff to exec signatures.

Gating notes: DPA must include the agreed retention & deletion language and a clear subprocessor disclosure mechanism; if either of those require exec sign-off on your side, we should surface that in the MAP so it doesn't block the 12/17 target.

I've attached a short clause checklist and a redlines cadence suggestion (dpa_clause_table_v2.docx). From Redwood's side, we can compress MSA redline turnaround to 3 business days for the core commercial terms if the DPA is on track.

Happy to hop on a 30-min alignment call 11/16 or 11/17 — suggest 9:30 PT on 11/16.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachments: dpa_clause_table_v2.docx
